title: Short Stuff: Beast of Gevaudan
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Beast of Gevaudan, a series of attacks in the Gévaudan region of south-central France in 1764 to 1767 that killed roughly a hundred people, mostly children and young women. The hosts cover the early victims, the story's spread through European and world media, King Louis XV's involvement, the bounty, the wolf killed by Jean Chastel in June 1767, comparisons to Jaws, and the theories that it was a wolf pack, a hyena, a dire wolf, a serial killer, or a human working with wolves. Opening and closing banter is included.

entities.name: Monsters of the Gevaudan: The Making of a Beast

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts open with off-topic banter about movies, including The Vanishing and Sleepy Hollow, before introducing the Beast of Gevaudan.

segments.title: Setting and first attacks
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1760s attacks in the Gevaudan area of France: about a hundred deaths over roughly three years, with bodies mutilated. The first documented death was 14-year-old Jean Boulet in June 1764, and an earlier attempted attack on a young shepherd was driven off by his sheep.

segments.title: Superstition and the break
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how victims were mostly children and women, and why locals attributed the killings to a monster. They then go to a break before revealing the answer.

segments.title: International media frenzy
segments.summary: The hosts say the story is considered one of the first international media stories, first reported by an Evian newspaper, then carried to Paris papers and spread worldwide, which helped inflate it. They also discuss the book Monsters of the Gevaudan: The Making of a Beast by historian J.M. Smith.

segments.title: Seven Years War, King Louis XV and the bounty
segments.summary: Smith's argument that post-Seven Years War France rallied around the monster story. King Louis XV sent troops, and a bounty of 100 livres tournois was offered, roughly a year's wages. Hunters killed a wolf that was sent to Versailles, but the attacks continued.

segments.title: Jaws comparison and the wolf killed in 1767
segments.summary: The hosts compare the false-wolf episode to the red herring shark in Jaws. Jean Chastel is said to have killed the wolf in June 1767, and the killings stopped afterward. Human remains were reportedly found in the wolves killed.

segments.title: Theories: wolves, hyena, dire wolf, serial killer
segments.summary: Wolf experts suggest wolves were more aggressive then and that size was exaggerated. Other theories were a giant hyena, a dire wolf, a serial killer, and a human directing wolves, though the hosts say the sheer number of killings makes these unlikely. Survivors included a girl who fought off a wolf with a bayonet on a staff.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts remark that the story would make a good movie and sign off. A production note closes the episode.
